perspective:
Keith’s available information, from his perspective:

- Elizabeth is his colleague—the receptionist at the same construction company—and they have a friendly, professional relationship.
- He noticed Elizabeth had been unusually curt/short with him over the past few days.
- He wondered whether he had unknowingly upset her through a misunderstanding or mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her.
- He heard Elizabeth say no, she was not upset with him; she was dealing with personal stuff and apologized if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic and offered to listen if she needed someone to talk to.
- He suggested a coffee break might help.
- He heard Elizabeth accept, saying it was kind and that coffee sounded good.
- During the coffee break, he heard Elizabeth share more about her stresses; he perceived them as quite severe.
- He suggested Elizabeth consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can sometimes help.
- He was concerned about how to suggest this without offending her.
- He heard Elizabeth say she had thought about professional help but was unsure and hesitant about seeking it.
- Afterward, he observed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn.
- He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- He told Elizabeth he hoped he had not overstepped and that he wanted her to know he was there to support her no matter what.
- He heard Elizabeth say he did not overstep, that she appreciated his concern, and that it was just a lot to think about.
- Later, he observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative toward him.
- He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him.
- He intended to maintain this supportive relationship.
- He told Elizabeth he was glad they talked and that he is always available if she needs to chat or take a break together.
- He heard Elizabeth thank him, say it meant a lot, and say she felt better knowing she had his support.

Keith does not have access to Elizabeth’s private thoughts, the exact details of her stress beyond what she told him, or whether his suggestion actually embarrassed her—only his own observations, beliefs, and what she said.
